{{Quote|Niin is who I ''was''&mdash;Darth Havok is who I ''am''.|Darth Havok|<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
'''Eshkar Niin''' was an [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] member of the [[Imperial Knight]]s, a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-using]] Order loyal to [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]] of the [[Fel Empire|Galactic Empire]]. Niin became a Master within the Order and the instructor of [[Antares Draco]], to whom he taught strategy and philosophy while training the [[Human/Legends|Human]] in the ways of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Niin later abandoned his vows as an Imperial Knight and deserted the Order. He [[Rooftop duel|attacked]] the Empress [[Elliah Fel]] and [[Death/Legends|killed]] her, but was subsequently defeated by Draco, who had been sent to kill him by the Emperor. Draco believed Niin to be dead, but the Iktotchi survived and joined [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[One Sith|Sith Order]], becoming the [[Sith Inquisitor]] '''Darth Havok'''. [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Krayt's Empire]] [[Attack on Emperor Fel|seized]] control of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] from Fel in [[130 ABY]], and [[137 ABY|seven years later]], a group of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] took Fel's daughter [[Marasiah Fel|Marasiah]] captive and brought her to the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. From there, Havok took her to the Sith [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and began [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] her, hoping to learn valuable secrets of her [[Parent/Legends|father's]].

In between interrogation sessions, Draco arrived on a [[Mission to Korriban (Second Imperial Civil War)|mission]] to rescue her and remained on-world to buy her [[Time/Legends|time]] as she escaped the planet. Havok confronted his former student and defeated him in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] before taking him [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] deep in the planet's dungeons. Havok inflicted agonizing torture on Draco in an effort to learn [[Empire-in-exile|Imperial]] secrets, and eventually used Draco's love for Marasiah to prompt the prisoner to reveal the existence of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Hidden Temple (Sith–Imperial War)|Hidden Temple]] on [[Taivas]]. Krayt's forces then [[Attack on the Hidden Temple|attacked]] the temple, but the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi]] and their allies evacuated and then [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|counterattacked]] at Coruscant. Krayt was slain, and his [[Darth Krayt's Sith trooper|Sith trooper]] [[Army/Legends|army]], whose members were linked to his will, went insane. Havok and several other Sith escaped from the mad [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] on Korriban and fled the planet, and Havok rendezvoused with [[Darth Nihl]], his new Master. Under Nihl's leadership, the Sith went into hiding.

==Biography==
===Knights of the Empire===
{{Quote|He knew strategy. He told me that a tiny fever wasp can carry death into places where a Krayt dragon cannot go.|Antares Draco, on Eshkar Niin's teachings|<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
[[File:Rooftopduel.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Eshkar Niin slays Empress Elliah Fel.]]
Prior to [[137 ABY]], the [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] Eshkar Niin was a member of the [[Imperial Knight]]s,<ref name="Legacy 49" /> an order of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]] dedicated to protecting [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]] and preserving his [[Fel Empire|Empire]].<ref name="lecg">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Niin was a Master both within the Order and of his pupil [[Antares Draco]], and he trained the young [[Human/Legends|Human]] as a Knight of the Empire. During his [[Time/Legends|time]] as an Imperial Knight, Niin constructed a [[Eshkar Niin's holocron|holocron]] and recorded some of his teachings within the [[Holocron/Legends|device]].<ref name="Legacy 49" /> He eventually abandoned his vows as an Imperial Knight and deserted the Order, prompting the Emperor to send Draco to [[Death/Legends|kill]] him.<ref name="Legacy 50">[[Legacy (2006) 50|''Legacy'' (2006) 50]]</ref>

Niin, meanwhile, tracked down Fel's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], the Empress [[Elliah Fel]], and both hunts culminated on a rooftop in a [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Skyscraper/Legends|skyscrapers]] as a three-way [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] [[Rooftop duel|broke out]]. Draco and Elliah both called on Niin to stop as he attacked the Empress, but he ignored their pleas and [[Telekinesis/Legends|shoved]] Draco away with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] before striking Elliah down. Draco immediately retaliated, and at the end of their duel, he believed Niin to be dead. Niin in fact survived, but allowed his former apprentice to remain confident of his demise.<ref name="Legacy War 2" /> The Imperial Knights thus thought that Niin,<ref name="Legacy 49" /><ref name="Legacy 50" /> the only member of their order to ever desert his vows,<ref name="Legacy 26">[[Legacy (2006) 26|''Legacy'' (2006) 26]]</ref> was dead.<ref name="Legacy 49" /><ref name="Legacy 50" />

===Inquisitor of the Sith===
{{Quote|My name is Darth Havok now. Try to remember that.|Darth Havok to Antares Draco|<ref name="Legacy 50" />}}
[[File:Havokspower.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Havok prevents Marasiah Fel from committing suicide during her torture.]]
After leaving the Imperial Knights, Niin joined the [[One Sith]] and became a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and [[Sith Inquisitor]] serving [[Darth Krayt]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]. He took the name [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Havok, abandoning his former identity.<ref name="Legacy 49" /><ref name="Legacy 48" /> In [[130 ABY]], Krayt [[Attack on Emperor Fel|seized]] [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] control from Emperor Fel,<ref name="Legacy 1">[[Legacy (2006) 1|''Legacy'' (2006) 1]]</ref> and seven [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, Fel's daughter [[Marasiah Fel|Marasiah]] was taken captive by several [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] who [[Operation: Thunderstroke|ambushed]] a group of Imperial Knights on [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]]. She was brought to the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the seat of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Krayt's Empire]]. Havok was ordered to take her to the Sith [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] by [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok]],<ref name="Legacy 48" /> who had been ruling the Empire since his attempted [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] of Krayt and usurping of the throne.<ref name="Legacy 31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref><ref name="Legacy 34">[[Legacy (2006) 34|''Legacy'' (2006) 34]]</ref>

Immediately after Marasiah exited the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] of her escort, [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Rulf Yage]], Havok approached them on their landing platform, concealing his identity from Marasiah with a hood. Despite protests from Imperial [[Regent/Legends|Regent]] [[Morlish Veed]], Havok took the [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] away from Yage and brought her to Korriban.<ref name="Legacy 48" /> Once there, Havok chained Marasiah up in the [[Chambers of Persuasion]] and began to [[Torture/Legends|torture]] her with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], hoping to glean secrets about her [[Parent/Legends|father's]] [[Empire-in-exile]]. She was resistant, however, prompting Havok to remove his hood and reveal his identity. Marasiah was shocked to see him alive, but shook off her surprise and telekinetically tossed a bowl of hot coals at him. Havok deflected the attack, but the distraction allowed Marasiah to seize his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] with the Force and place it beneath her chin, hoping to die rather than talk. Havok drew on the Force himself and took the weapon back.<ref name="Legacy 49" /> He then left the chamber to allow his prisoner some recovery time.<ref name="Legacy 50" />

While Havok was away, Antares Draco, fellow Imperial Knight [[Ganner Krieg]], and the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Shado Vao]] arrived at the chambers on a [[Mission to Korriban (Second Imperial Civil War)|mission]] to rescue the [[Princess/Legends|Princess]], and they freed her from her bonds. Draco remained on-world to allow his allies time to flee the planet in their escape ship, and Havok approached him as he was slaughtering a group of Sith. As they engaged each other in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], Darth Krayt, alive and well, projected his will across the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Both Havok and Draco were drawing on the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] and felt his call. Havok offered Draco a chance to join the Sith, but when the Imperial Knight refused, Havok shocked him with Force lightning. Draco's presence was severed from the Force,<ref name="Legacy 50" /> and, defeated, he became Havok's prisoner.<ref name="Legacy War 1">[[Legacy — War 1|''Legacy — War'' 1]]</ref>

===Breaking Draco===
{{Quote|Put Master Draco back into the bacta to heal. Can't have him dying before he tells us his secrets. And he ''will'' tell those secrets. I was his Master when I was an Imperial Knight&mdash;and I know where my former apprentice is most vulnerable.|Havok to a Sith acolyte, while torturing Draco|<ref name="Legacy War 1" />}}
[[File:Measureofoblivion.jpg|thumb|left|210px|Havok tortures Antares Draco.]]
Deep in Korriban's dungeons, Havok subjected Draco to agonizing torture, using the Force to slice his body with shards of [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]]. Draco refused to divulge Imperial secrets, insisting that he would rather die; Havok gave him periodic rest in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] to ensure that he remained alive long enough to reveal the information that Havok sought. Having trained Draco in the ways of the Force, Havok knew Draco's vulnerabilities,<ref name="Legacy War 1" /> and created a [[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusion|Force illusion]] that took his former apprentice back to the day that Elliah Fel had died. As Draco relived the duel, Havok appealed to his guilt and claimed that he had been too weak to save her. Havok then projected another illusion onto his fellow Sith Lord [[Darth Talon]], making her appear to be Marasiah Fel. He told Draco that Vao and Krieg had been killed during their escape from Korriban and that Marasiah had been recaptured, and Talon planted a kiss on Draco's lips to promote the deception. When Havok threatened to kill her if Draco did not tell him any valuable information, Draco lost his resolve and revealed the existence of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Hidden Temple (Sith–Imperial War)|Hidden Temple]] on [[Taivas]]. Talon left to relay the findings to Darth Krayt, now back in control of the Empire, and Havok continued to torture Draco with Force lightning.<ref name="Legacy War 2" />

Talon delivered Draco to Krayt's nemesis, [[Cade Skywalker]], whom Krayt hoped to entice into a confrontation. The [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] and its allies gathered to [[Attack on the Hidden Temple|defend]] the Hidden Temple from Krayt's forces,<ref name="Legacy War 3">[[Legacy — War 3|''Legacy — War'' 3]]</ref> and there, the Dark Lord unleashed upon them his secret [[Army/Legends|army]] of [[Darth Krayt's Sith trooper|Sith troopers]], dark warriors who were linked to his will.<ref name="Legacy War 4">[[Legacy — War 4|''Legacy — War'' 4]]</ref> After the allies evacuated Taivas, they launched a [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|counterstrike]] at Coruscant that saw Krayt die at Skywalker's hands. The Dark Lord's death saw Sith troopers across the galaxy go mad, and the Sith forces at Coruscant killed many of them before fleeing the capital. On Korriban, many Sith died at the hands of the insane troopers, but Havok and several others evacuated. Havok rendezvoused with [[Darth Nihl]], Krayt's ''de facto'' successor, elsewhere in the galaxy, and Nihl instructed him to hide what was left of the Sith [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]]. Krayt's Empire was fractured, and the Sith would now disperse themselves throughout the galaxy, infiltrate planetary governments, and wait for their opportunity to strike from the shadows.<ref name="Legacy War 6">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|When I am through, if you have not become insane, you will wish I had let you kill yourself. You will wish your life was a switch you could just turn off&hellip; But first, you must learn&mdash;Princess&mdash;just who is the ''Master'' here!|Havok, to Marasiah Fel|<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
Before joining the Sith, Eshkar Niin had [[Color/Legends|brown]] skin<ref name="Legacy War 2">[[Legacy — War 2|''Legacy — War'' 2]]</ref> and dark [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]; afterward, Darth Havok had fiery yellow eyes and [[Sith tattoo]]s in black and red. As an Imperial Knight, Niin was recognized for his knowledge of strategy. He taught Draco a parable involving a [[Fever wasp/Legends|fever wasp]] and a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]], informing his pupil that a small fever wasp could bring death to places where a large krayt dragon was unable.<ref name="Legacy 49" /> He also instructed Draco to always ensure that a slain opponent was definitely dead.<ref name="Legacy 50" /> Niin eventually left the Order, believing that the ways of the Sith were where his destiny lay.<ref name="Legacy 49" /><ref name="Legacy 50" /> When he later dueled Draco on Korriban, he hoped to recruit his former student into the Sith's ranks rather than kill him. He struck Draco with Force lightning when the offer was refused.<ref name="Legacy 50" /> Havok was loyal to Darth Krayt,<ref name="Legacy War 2" /> but he accepted Darth Nihl as his new Master following Krayt's death and addressed Nihl as "My Lord."<ref name="Legacy War 6" />

As a Sith Inquisitor, Darth Havok tortured information out of prisoners, inflicting pain on them until they wished for death. In addition to subjecting his charges to physical torture, he employed mind games in his interrogation, such as when he caused Marasiah Fel to doubt the honesty of Antares Draco.<ref name="Legacy 49" /> When he later tortured Draco, he used his knowledge of his former student's vulnerabilities and used Force illusions to appeal to Draco's guilt over not having saved Empress Elliah Fel. He eventually got Draco to talk by making him believe that Marasiah's life was in danger, but continued to torture his subject even after receiving valuable information.<ref name="Legacy War 2" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|I am much changed, Princess. Much stronger in the dark side than I ever was in the light.|Havok, to Marasiah Fel|<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
[[File:Whenyouplaywithfire.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Havok deflects a telekinetic attack made by Marasiah Fel.]]
Eshkar Niin was a Master within the Imperial Knights,<ref name="Legacy 49" /> an organization that was said to be among the most talented and dangerous Force-users in the galaxy. The title of Master was reserved for its highest-ranking members.<ref name="lecg" /> After he deserted the Order, however, he was bested by his former student Antares Draco during a confrontation and was believed to be dead.<ref name="Legacy 50" />

As a Sith Lord, Darth Havok was able to use telekinesis to counter and overpower Marasiah Fel's own telekinetic exertion;<ref name="Legacy 49" /> she herself was a fully-trained Imperial Knight.<ref name="Legacy 23">[[Legacy (2006) 23|''Legacy'' (2006) 23]]</ref> He could also create Force lightning and used it to defeat Antares Draco,<ref name="Legacy 50" /> an Imperial Knight Master.<ref name="Legacy 0½">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0½|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0½]]</ref> Havok was proficient in the art of creating Force illusions, and employed them while torturing his subjects.<ref name="Legacy War 2" />

==Behind the scenes==
Darth Havok was created by [[John Ostrander]] and [[Jan Duursema]] for the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' and first appeared in its [[Legacy (2006) 48|forty-eighth]] issue.<ref name="Legacy 48" />
